disease_sections.title: Oxidative Stress
disease_sections.overview: Oxidative stress occurs when harmful free radicals outweigh the body's antioxidant defenses, leading to gradual damage of cells and tissues. Over time, this imbalance may contribute to aging and increase the risk of several chronic diseases.

current_status.interpretation: Your score is still healthy but nearing the upper end of this range. Improving lifestyle quality now can reduce future oxidative stress.
current_status.clinical_warning: Persistent symptoms or multiple abnormal metabolic markers should be discussed with your healthcare provider.

exercise: Complete at least 150 minutes of aerobic activity weekly.

recommendations: Prefer healthy fats from fish and nuts.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Small improvements now can help keep oxidative stress low over time.

disease_sections.title: Hypertension
disease_sections.overview: Hypertension is a condition in which blood pressure remains consistently higher than normal, placing increased strain on the heart and blood vessels. Uncontrolled hypertension can cause organ damage over time and increase the risk of heart disease, stroke, and kidney issues.

current_status.interpretation: Your profile remains within the healthy range, but there is less margin for preventable risk. Strengthening healthy habits now can help maintain normal blood pressure and reduce future cardiovascular risk.
current_status.clinical_warning: Arrange a medical review if your blood pressure remains consistently elevated. Seek urgent care if severe symptoms such as chest pain, breathlessness, confusion, or sudden weakness occur.

exercise: Aim for 150–300 minutes of moderate aerobic activity each week.
Include strength training at least twice weekly.
Stretch regularly and avoid prolonged sitting.

recommendations: Follow a DASH-style diet rich in vegetables, fruits, and whole grains.
Choose fresh foods over processed options.
Include potassium-rich foods unless advised otherwise.
Check your blood pressure during routine health visits.
Monitor your weight and waist circumference.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Small, consistent lifestyle improvements can help maintain healthy blood pressure and protect your heart.

disease_sections.title: Type 2 diabetes
disease_sections.overview: Type 2 diabetes is a metabolic disorder in which the body becomes resistant to insulin or does not produce enough insulin to maintain healthy blood sugar levels. Persistently elevated blood glucose can damage the eyes, kidneys, nerves, heart, and blood vessels over time.

current_status.interpretation: Your blood sugar remains well controlled, with only minor markers worth monitoring over time.

recommendations: Base meals on vegetables and legumes.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Small healthy habits today help preserve long-term metabolic health.

disease_sections.title: Obesity
disease_sections.overview: Obesity is a chronic condition characterized by excessive body fat accumulation that can affect overall health. It may result from genetic, lifestyle, environmental, and metabolic factors, and can increase the risk of conditions such as diabetes, heart disease, and hypertension.

current_status.interpretation: You remain in the healthy range, but reinforcing healthy habits now helps prevent future weight gain.
current_status.clinical_warning: Persistent weight gain should be discussed with your healthcare provider.

exercise: At least 150 minutes of aerobic exercise weekly.

recommendations: Continue glucose, blood pressure, and lipid screening.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Strengthening healthy habits now protects your long-term health.

disease_sections.title: NAFLD
disease_sections.overview: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) is a condition where excess fat builds up in the liver in people who drink little or no alcohol, commonly linked to obesity, diabetes, and metabolic syndrome. If left untreated, it can progress from simple fatty liver to inflammation, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and even liver failure.

current_status.interpretation: Your liver health remains reassuring with minimal evidence of fat accumulation. Consistent healthy habits will help preserve this favorable profile.
current_status.clinical_warning: Routine care is sufficient unless symptoms develop or liver tests become abnormal.

exercise: Complete at least 150 minutes of aerobic exercise weekly.

recommendations: Choose whole fruit instead of fruit juice.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Your liver remains healthy, and consistent habits will help keep it that way.

disease_sections.title: Thyroid Health
disease_sections.overview: The thyroid gland produces hormones that regulate metabolism, energy production, body temperature, and many essential body functions. Changes in thyroid function can affect multiple organs and influence weight, heart rate, mood, and overall metabolic health.

current_status.interpretation: Your thyroid-related metabolic profile appears excellent, with little evidence of increased risk. Continue your current healthy habits to maintain normal thyroid function.
current_status.clinical_warning: No specific thyroid concerns are suggested. Seek medical advice only if new symptoms develop.

recommendations: Consider thyroid testing only if symptoms develop.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Your thyroid health appears well supported by your current lifestyle.

disease_sections.title: Dyslipidemia
disease_sections.overview: Dyslipidemia is a condition in which the levels of cholesterol or triglycerides in the blood become unhealthy. If left unmanaged, it can gradually increase the risk of heart attack, stroke, and other cardiovascular diseases.

current_status.interpretation: Your cholesterol and triglyceride levels are excellent, supporting a healthy heart and blood vessels.

Choose olive oil, nuts, and oily fish.
Check your cholesterol during routine health visits.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Your cholesterol profile is excellent—keep up your healthy habits.
